faqs.q: When was South-View Cemetery founded?
faqs.a: South-View Cemetery was chartered on April 26, 1886, by six formerly enslaved African American men in Atlanta, Georgia.

faqs.q: Who founded South-View Cemetery?
faqs.a: South-View was founded by Albert Watts, Jacob McKinley, George W. Graham, Robert Grant, Charles H. Morgan, and John Render — all formerly enslaved African Americans.

faqs.q: Why was South-View Cemetery created?
faqs.a: South-View was created because of the indignities African Americans faced at Atlanta's segregated cemeteries — particularly Oakland Cemetery's 'Slave Square' (whose occupants were mass-exhumed in 1877) and Westview's segregated 'Rest Haven.' Albert Watts was moved to action after watching his father buried through Westview's back gate in October 1885.

faqs.q: Is Martin Luther King Jr. buried at South-View Cemetery?
faqs.a: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was temporarily buried at South-View in 1968 after his assassination, but his remains were later moved to the MLK Center for Nonviolent Social Change in Atlanta. However, his parents — Rev. Martin Luther King Sr. and Alberta Williams King — ARE permanently interred at South-View in a marble crypt.

faqs.q: How many people are buried at South-View?
faqs.a: More than 70,000 people are buried at South-View, with hundreds of new burials each year.

faqs.q: Where is South-View Cemetery located?
faqs.a: South-View Cemetery is at 1990 Jonesboro Road SE, Atlanta, Georgia 30315, in the Lakewood Heights neighborhood — about 15 minutes from downtown Atlanta.

faqs.q: What are South-View Cemetery's hours?
faqs.a: South-View is open Monday through Sunday, 9:00am to 5:00pm. Phone: (404) 622-5393.

faqs.q: Is South-View an active cemetery?
faqs.a: Yes. South-View is an active cemetery with thousands of burial spaces available and undeveloped land to keep it operational for decades.

faqs.q: What is South-View's historical significance?
faqs.a: South-View is the oldest African American cemetery in Atlanta and the oldest African American non-eleemosynary (non-charitable) stockholder corporation in the United States. It has served as the final resting place for over 70,000 African Americans from Reconstruction to the present, documenting the full sweep of Black Atlanta history.

faqs.q: Who is Alonzo Herndon?
faqs.a: Alonzo Franklin Herndon was born into slavery but became Atlanta's first Black millionaire. He established a chain of successful barbershops and founded the Atlanta Life Insurance Company. He is buried at South-View Cemetery.

faqs.q: Can I take a tour of South-View Cemetery?
faqs.a: Yes. South-View offers docent-led walking tours of notable gravesites, group tours by reservation, and a free self-guided cell phone walking/driving tour.

faqs.q: Who was Georgia's first Black registered nurse?
faqs.a: Ludie Clay Andrews (d. 1969) was the first African American registered nurse in Georgia. She organized the Grady Municipal Training School for Colored Nurses in 1914. She is buried at South-View.

faqs.q: Who was Georgia's first Black licensed pharmacist?
faqs.a: Moses Amos (d. 1928) passed the Georgia state pharmacy exam in June 1911 and became the first African American granted a druggist license by the Georgia State Board of Pharmacy. He is buried at South-View.

faqs.q: What was WERD radio station?
faqs.a: WERD was the first radio station in the United States owned by African Americans. Jesse Bee Blayton (d. 1977) — Georgia's first Black CPA and a Mutual Federal Savings founder — purchased WERD in 1949. Blayton is buried at South-View.

faqs.q: Who was Grace Towns Hamilton?
faqs.a: Grace Towns Hamilton (d. 1992) was the first African American woman elected as a state legislator in the Deep South. She served in the Georgia legislature from 1965 to 1984 and was a principal architect of the 1973 Atlanta city charter. She is buried at South-View.

faqs.q: Is South-View Cemetery on the National Register of Historic Places?
faqs.a: South-View was listed on the Georgia Register of Historic Places in 2026 and a National Register of Historic Places nomination was submitted (NPS reference BC100013186). The nomination was coordinated with the Atlanta Preservation Center.

faqs.q: Which Atlanta Child Murder victims are buried at South-View?
faqs.a: Seven victims of the 1979-1981 Atlanta Child Murders are buried at South-View: Milton Harvey, Yusef Bell, Aaron Wyche, Aaron Jackson, Patrick Rogers, Curtis Walker, and William Barrett.

faqs.q: What athletes are buried at South-View?
faqs.a: Notable athletes include Walter Jones Bellamy (1960 Olympic gold medalist, 1962 NBA Rookie of the Year, Basketball Hall of Fame 1993), David T. Harper (Negro League outfielder), and Hank Aaron (baseball legend).

faqs.q: Who manages South-View Cemetery?
faqs.a: South-View is managed by the South-View Cemetery Association. The Watts family has managed it from its earliest days. As of 2018, president Winifred Watts Hemphill is the great-granddaughter of founder Albert Watts.

faqs.q: What is the Historic South-View Preservation Foundation?
faqs.a: The Historic South-View Preservation Foundation is a nonprofit founded in 2004. It records, interprets, restores, and preserves the art, history, and environment of South-View's non-perpetual care sections. Historian D.L. Henderson joined its board in 2005 and wrote the 2018 book 'South-View: City of the Dead.'

faqs.q: Who is John Wesley Dobbs?
faqs.a: John Wesley Dobbs was a well-known Atlanta civic and political leader known as the 'Mayor of Sweet Auburn.' He is buried at South-View. His daughter Mattiwilda Dobbs was the first African American to sing a major role at Italy's La Scala opera house.

faqs.q: What book is this database based on?
faqs.a: This database is sourced from 'South-View: City of the Dead' by D.L. Henderson, published by Carrelspin Press, Dunwoody, Georgia, in 2018. ISBN 978-0-9985772-0-3. Henderson served as South-View's historian and developed its first public walking tour.

faqs.q: Who is Bishop Henry McNeal Turner?
faqs.a: Bishop Henry McNeal Turner was a prominent African Methodist Episcopal (AME) Church leader and a Reconstruction-era Georgia state legislator. He is buried at South-View and is quoted as saying: 'There is no such place as a white heaven.'

faqs.q: What is the Founders Mausoleum at South-View?
faqs.a: The Founders Mausoleum opened at South-View Cemetery on August 1, 2009. It offers families an above-ground burial option.

faqs.q: What were Slave Square and Rest Haven?
faqs.a: Slave Square was the segregated African American burial section at Oakland Cemetery (est. 1850), with 860+ burials by the Civil War's end. In 1877, the Atlanta City Council voted to exhume and mass-reinter its occupants to resell the land. Rest Haven was the segregated African American section at Westview Cemetery (est. 1884), accessible only through a back gate. Both were direct causes of South-View's founding.
